code.originalText: Day 1 of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir: drug interaction check, carvedilol titration, glucose monitoring, vitamin D, and the bone density plan

text.paragraph: First day of hepatitis C treatment. [S]

Mr. Knievel returns four weeks after the hepatology visit to start sofosbuvir-velpatasvir, which has been approved. He takes carvedilol 6.25 mg daily without dizziness. He has had one drink in the past month and wants to stop altogether. He started aquatic therapy three weeks ago and walks a little farther; pain is about 5 of 10. He has taken no omeprazole, ibuprofen or herbal products. He has had no low glucose readings, abdominal swelling, black stools, confusion or yellow eyes. He has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1996-02-23; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 84.8 kg; blood pressure 128/78, pulse 68
Spider angiomas unchanged; no jaundice or bruising
Reduced hip rotation; knee crepitus; old forearm fracture deformities

Raised transaminases (ALT 88, AST 96 U/L) and low platelets (118) on today's tests, with spider angiomas and palmar erythema, in a man of 57 who received many blood transfusions after crashes before 1962 and drinks most evenings: chronic liver disease, most likely hepatitis C, must be excluded. Hepatitis C antibody with reflex RNA, hepatitis A and B serology, HIV, liver ultrasound and hepatology review ordered
S — Synthetic presenting problem; no symptom or result of his real illness was made public. Superseded at the hepatology consultation.

Chronic hepatitis C, genotype 1a, treatment-naive, HCV RNA 2.35 million IU/mL, likely acquired through blood transfusions after crashes; synthetic modern detail linked to his publicly reported transfusion-acquired hepatitis C
S — Synthetic genotype, viral load and timing; his hepatitis C and its likely transfusion source are documented (D).

Compensated cirrhosis from hepatitis C, with alcohol as a cofactor: liver stiffness 26.8 kPa, FIB-4 4.94, nodular liver and a 14.2 cm spleen on ultrasound, platelets 118; Child-Pugh A5, MELD-Na 8; no ascites, encephalopathy, jaundice or bleeding
S — Synthetic stage of liver disease linked to his documented hepatitis C and later liver transplant.
Clinically significant portal hypertension in compensated cirrhosis (liver stiffness 25 kPa or more), treated with carvedilol without screening endoscopy (Baveno VII)
S — Synthetic finding at the hepatology consultation.
S — Synthetic; diabetes is documented only in his last years (D), and placing it at 57 is a synthetic choice.
Chronic pain in the back, hips, pelvis and knees after dozens of fractures from stunt crashes, including a broken pelvis; ibuprofen stopped, and managed without oral NSAIDs or opioids
S — Synthetic pain at the index age, anchored to his documented fractures and the pain of his later years.

list.item:
Chronic hepatitis C, genotype 1a (B18.2). Pre-treatment tests within three months are complete: platelets 121, creatinine 0.90 mg/dL with eGFR 100, ALT 81, AST 90 U/L, bilirubin 1.0 mg/dL, albumin 3.7 g/dL, and INR 1.1 in January. The interaction check is unchanged. On-treatment liver tests are optional on this pathway; he will call for jaundice, dark urine or abdominal swelling. As the virus clears, glucose can fall, so he will watch his sensor for lows. [S]
Sofosbuvir-velpatasvir one tablet daily from today for 12 weeks; a pill box and phone reminder.
Review at the end of treatment.
No new medicines or supplements without checking.

Clinically significant portal hypertension (K76.6). Pulse 68 and blood pressure 128/78 on carvedilol 6.25 mg allow the target dose. [S]
Carvedilol 12.5 mg daily from today.
Hold a dose and call if systolic pressure falls below 90 or he feels faint.

Vitamin D deficiency (E55.9). 25-hydroxyvitamin D 17 ng/mL, common in cirrhosis; calcium 9.1 mg/dL and TSH 2.1 are normal; vitamin B12 388 pg/mL on long-term metformin is normal. [S]
Vitamin D3 1970 units daily.
Bone density scan in two weeks.
Recheck vitamin D at the end of treatment.

Type 2 diabetes (E11.65). Glucose 141 mg/dL fasting; sensor started today. [S]
Continue metformin.
Sensor review at the end of treatment.

Chronic pain from old fractures (G89.29). Better with aquatic therapy; no NSAIDs or opioids. [S]
Continue aquatic therapy twice a week and the home program.
Acetaminophen up to 2 g a day; diclofenac gel to the knees.
